name: Orange OR120 Graphic MkII (1972, 120 W, 4 x EL34)
description: The 1972 Orange OR120 Graphic MkII: two identical 68k inputs -> V1A (220k/2k2+50u) -> 68n -> passive bass/treble stack with a 330p bright cap across the gain pot -> GAIN -> V1B (220k/2k2+50u) -> 68n -> FAC (6-position stepped low cut: a 4n7/4n7/2n2/1n/330p series chain tapped by the rotor) -> 100k -> V2A driver (100k plate load bypassed by 1n, unbypassed 1k5 cathode carrying the BOOST choke trap and the 15k global feedback from the 16 ohm tap) -> 68n -> V2B cathodyne (100k plate, 1k5+100k cathode with the 1M grid leak to the 1k5/100k junction) -> 68n/68n -> 4 x EL34, 2k4 stoppers, 1k screens, 220k grid leaks to the N.B rail -> OT 16 ohm (the impedance selector is drawn on 16), feedback from the same tap. Supply: 8 x 1N4005 bridge (2 per leg), 2 x 100u/450V reservoir + 100k balances, choke to the screens (2 x 32u/450V), 33k + 33k to the PI and preamp rails (16u each). Bias: its own winding -> 1N4005 -> 2 x 22u/63V + 22k -> 1k -> N.B. Effects loop (SEND/RETURN through 100k each) modelled normalled. 1972-only features kept: 2 mH boost choke, the cathodyne bias pair, 2k4 grid stoppers, FAC order.

io.note: outputVoltsPerFS = 1.5 x 55.5 V, the measured dimed fundamental peak speaker voltage at the -46.9 V bias (notes S8); was 86 at the earlier -37 V bias

controls.label: FAC (Lo Cut)
controls.note: Frequency Analyzing Control: 6-position rotary that taps a series chain of 4n7, 4n7, 2n2, 1n, 330p between the preamp output and the 100k into V2A's grid. Stud 1 = direct (no low cut); measured -3 dB corners for studs 2-6: 107, 207, 427, 937, 2543 Hz (the drawn chain against the real source impedance, not the 220k leak alone). Default 0.25 = stud 2 (the mildest cut; the selector value is normalised 0..1 over the six studs, measured). The legacy 0..0.79611 param range is mapped linearly over the six studs

controls.label: H.F. Drive
controls.note: VC4 '1k Lin BOOST' - the panel's H.F. DRIVE: a 1k lin pot across V2A's unbypassed 1k5 cathode, its wiper feeding a 2 mH + 0.47u series trap to ground (5.2 kHz)

parts.label: Bias reservoir (ideal source, library convention)
parts.note: power sheet OR120_72power.jpg: the 1972 bias is its own centre-tapped winding (620..700 x 700..800, no voltage printed) -> two 1N4005 (full wave, CT to the return rail) -> first 22u/63V (stem x=972) -> 1k -> second 22u/63V + 22k bleeder -> N.B. Jacobs's page gives the winding as 72 V, i.e. 36-0-36 V for this two-diode CT rectifier: 36 V RMS = 51 V peak, about -50 V at the first reservoir less the diode drop and the 22k+1k load. Set to -49 V so N.B = -49 x 22k/23k = -46.9 V, the grid voltage an owner measured on a late-1971/early-1972 fixed-bias OR120 (forum.orangeamps.com t=43647: '-46.9v' after the 220k grid leaks, no bias pot); a later OR120 measured -46 V (t=7331). Modelled as an ideal source at the first reservoir (a negative-peak rectifier is uncharged at the crest operating point the SPICE gate uses). Idle with this bias: 39.9 mA, 20.6 W per EL34 (card). The 1974 Musonic sheet's 'ADJUST BIAS TO -37VDC' belongs to its adjustable 100k-pot network at A = 480 V / B = 470 V and is not this circuit. Hickmott's added ground on the bias return is used (his own comment on the sheet)

parts.label: Output transformer, 16/8/4 ohm
parts.note: output sheet OR120_72output.jpg: A+ centre tap (1713,668) on the reservoir node a; primary halves to the plates; secondary wound 0 -> 4 ohm (t4, y=649) -> 8 ohm (t8, y=495) -> 16 ohm (spk, y=345), phased so the 15k feedback is negative (the sheet prints no dot convention; with the primaries as drawn the opposite secondary phase closes a REGENERATIVE loop, measured: |loop gain| 1.7 at 1 kHz and a 37 Hz limit cycle); the impedance selector's blade is drawn on the 16 ohm stud (2047,610) so only 16 is loaded. Fitted: no OT data is printed. unverified: the sheet prints no OT data - Raa 1.75k, DCR, leak, lm, lsat taken from the same-era 4xEL34 library figure (hiwatt-dr103)
